payload.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-runtime-evidence.ts:1-12 claims a Finding-owned two-command runtime-evidence handler facade, but line 7 aliases createFindingLedgerHandlers wholesale; that factory also returns finding_ledger_query, while the facade itself is consumed only by the immutable RED test and is not wired by packages/main/src/registry.ts or exported by packages/main/src/index.ts/package exports. The acknowledged expansion therefore does not establish the promised narrow/public runtime command boundary and can leak Ledger Query responsibility if later registered. Replace the alias with a narrow wrapper that returns exactly finding_runtime_evidence_run and finding_runtime_evidence_verify and wire/export the intended boundary, or remove the public-boundary promise/expansion with proof that the direct registered ledger handler is the canonical contract.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:569 display-ID allocation still uses findings.length + 1, so a sparse legacy set such as F-001/F-003 allocates F-003 again; lines 632-634 then find the old row by display ID and neither replace nor append when recordId differs, silently hiding the newly durable ledger record from readFindings. This preserves the historical ID-reuse/vanishing-row failure despite globally unique recordIds.

packages/main/src/core/store.ts:486-499 overwrites a matching findings.json row with the original append-only ledger finding payload whenever recordId matches. finding_resolve only updates findings.json at handlers/finding.ts:821-843 and appends no ledger status mutation. At HEAD 591642d, commits e93c480 and 591642d are finding_resolve metadata commits, yet proof-or-stop finding_list --storyId=B-fe8f --json still returns F-001 and F-002 status=open. Thus resolution/dismissal is reverted on read, making user output and lifecycle consumers observe stale open state and invalidating exactly-once historical correction. Add append-only status-transition records/current projection plus a regression that resolves and rereads a ledger-backed Finding.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:821-843 — finding_resolve still mutates only the findings.json compatibility mirror via readFindings/writeFindings and never appends a fenced ledger status-transition/successor record. The repository itself now demonstrates the lost update: commit e93c480257 resolves F-001, then commit 591642d288 resolves F-002 while reverting F-001 from resolved back to open; current finding_list confirms F-001 is open. This violates Story 3 objective that every Finding-system mutation be durable/exactly-once and lets concurrent closeouts resurrect a gate-consumed finding. Route resolve/dismiss status transitions through one append-only, idempotent fenced ledger transaction, derive the compatibility projection from the ledger, and add a concurrent two-finding resolve regression proving both resolutions survive and replay returns the original transition IDs.

packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:131-155 — the new dependency gate releases a prerequisite solely when dependency.phase === DONE; it never proves the dependency branch is merged into local main/current baseline. packages/main/src/core/partial-done-recovery.ts:123-151 explicitly models the real failure state phase=DONE while story/<id> is not an ancestor of main, so phase alone is not the accepted DONE-and-merged contract. The smoke fixture compounds this by directly writeStory(... phase:DONE) and calling the dependency released, which cannot prove merged-state behavior. A partial-DONE dependency can therefore authorize dependent DEV before its APIs exist on main. Fail closed on both canonical DONE and a mechanical merge/ancestry (or equivalent signed merged-capability) proof, and mutate the merge fact independently in the dependency regression.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:632-858 / current B-fe8f ledger — the delivered public query does not work against the Story that produced it: `proof-or-stop finding_ledger_query --storyId=B-fe8f` on current HEAD fails closed with `finding-ledger-query:ledger_receipt_unsigned`. The smoke proves only fresh synthetic ledgers, while B-fe8f contains earlier in-Story ledger receipts that the final verifier cannot consume. CHK-005 promises a stable signed query for ledger/CAS/idempotency/runtime/migration inputs and Story 2 depends on that public port; an unreadable canonical ledger cannot satisfy it. Add a bounded append-only migration/legacy-binding path (without rewriting committed semantic bytes), prove the current real B-fe8f ledger becomes queryable, and retain negative rejection for genuinely unsigned/tampered post-migration rows.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:386-417,432-481 validates only the proposal top-level key set and shallow variant shape. It never requires FindingRef.recordId, the required dependencyBundle members, non-empty current witness receipts, or a truthful proposalSigner algorithm/keyId/trustRoot; receipt currentness rejects only the explicit boolean false, so an omitted result is accepted. Repro after rebuilding dist: a correctly Ed25519-signed proposal with findingRef missing recordId, dependencyBundle={}, currentWitness.receiptIds=[], and proposalSigner.algorithm="rsa"/empty keyId/trustRoot returns {valid:true}. This contradicts the immutable exact-union, named signer/trust, dependency-bundle, and non-current-receipt fail-closed contract.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:886-927,1107-1124,1131-1147,1232-1251 derives both the runtime signer and its fresh key status solely from the same invocation environment. A caller can generate a new keypair, set PROOF_OR_STOP_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_PRIVATE_KEY/PUBLIC_KEY, mint a receipt, and have that same unpersisted key treated as current; it can also omit the caller-controlled revoked-key env to remove revocation. finding_ledger_query additionally accepts caller-supplied trustedKeys. The production smoke itself generates a fresh key at tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:808-838 and immediately persists a valid receipt, proving there is no independent repository trust/rotation registry. This makes signer freshness and revocation self-asserted rather than verifier-derived.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:994-1005,1131-1165 checks the canonical proper-lockfile mutex once, then runs build/execution under a different Story runtime mkdir lock. The canonical mutex is neither acquired nor rechecked at commit. Deterministic repro: pause the adapter inside its buildCommand after the initial check, acquire scripts/build-lock.mjs withBuildLock(root), resume while holding that canonical lock through CLI exit; finding_runtime_evidence_run exits 0 and persists a runtime_evidence_receipt. Thus a build that starts in the check-to-run window is accepted, so the build-in-progress refusal is not one atomic boundary with receipt production.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:561-652 makes the ledger/mirror append idempotent, but lines 677-705 unconditionally append reviewer_finding and recompute/write metrics after every replay, outside the ledger transaction and without the idempotency key. Focused synthetic-repo repro calls finding_add twice with identical bytes and idempotencyKey: the ledger has 1 record/1 receipt while process-events contains 2 reviewer_finding rows. Therefore CLI retry is not exactly-once across its durable audit side effects and can make the event history disagree with the canonical transaction count.

packages/main/src/core/evidence/artifact-store.ts:59-66,83-103 performs realpath containment once, then reuses the unresolved logical dir for exists/read, openSync(temp), renameSync(destination), and directory fsync. There is no held directory descriptor, no no-follow/openat-style operation, and no lock covering the containment check through publication. A local symlink/directory swap after line 85 therefore makes the later path components resolve outside the project even though the initial check passed; the current smoke at tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:1134-1148 covers only a symlink already present before the check. This leaves the required symlink-swap/path-escape fail-closed boundary unproved and permits out-of-root blob publication in the race window.

CHK-001 has no admissible current GREEN receipt. At HEAD 723f2ab, the immutable RED blob is still 1b913dab2f52e904afc1b7b1870a3a98be0739bc, but its pinned command `node packages/main/tests/red/red-bfe8f-ledger-runtime-integrity.mjs` exits 1 at line 212 because the accepted sparse allocator no longer matches the pre-GREEN length-based sentinel. The GREEN smoke explicitly expects that non-zero exit at finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:467-483, while all 13 CHK-001 verificationEvidence rows say result=pass/fresh for the direct RED command; CHK-001:happy:2 is additionally mechanical=false with no receipt. `proof-or-stop evidence_plan` nevertheless classifies all 71 rows fresh. Repair the intent/evidence relation with an executable superseding current command and per-intent exitCode=0/selectorMatched=true receipts; do not restamp the old output or weaken the immutable RED.

CHK-006:happy:5 proves only an already-installed global binary, not the publishable package. Independent clean-install repro `npm pack ./packages/main --ignore-scripts` followed by `npm install <proof-or-stop-core-0.3.270.tgz>` fails E404 for `@lattice/lab@0.3.65`. packages/main/package.json:126 still depends on the retired package name and packages/lab/package.json:2 still declares `@lattice/lab`; the registry has neither that package nor `@proof-or-stop/lab`. Therefore the changed CLI cannot be clean-installed and no installed CLI gate can execute from the produced tarball. Rename/publish or bundle/link the lab dependency under the accepted proof-or-stop namespace, update lockfiles, and add a temp-directory pack+clean-install+`proof-or-stop --version` plus Story-3 command-availability smoke.

Finding display and durable identities no longer derive uniqueness from mutable array length; fenced ledger append proves 100 concurrent unique rows and collision-free record IDs on the current HEAD.
